text:
Marathon Petroleum fell 2.5% today, extending a two-week slide of 14%, as oil prices retreated and geopolitical risk in the Middle East remained elevated but contained. US crude dropped to $82.24 per barrel—down sharply from earlier this month—while refineries are running at a high 97.5% capacity utilization, leaving little room for margin expansion. The combination of lower crude costs and limited ability to push throughput higher weighs on refiner profitability.

The broader backdrop hasn't improved the investment case. Attacks on Saudi and Russian energy infrastructure, Iranian tanker incidents in the Hormuz Strait, and ongoing Ukraine-Russia energy warfare keep Middle Eastern supply disruptions in the headlines, yet oil prices have still fallen—suggesting markets expect global demand to remain soft or supply concerns to ease. Meanwhile, US crude is trading at a significant $9.56 discount to world oil, which limits the arbitrage advantage domestic refiners typically enjoy.
